title: Notes on Hot Pot Bureau
summary: A hot pot party last weekend reminded me of the friendships I have built over the past year because of my children. From the accidental acquaintance while walking the baby downstairs last year, to camping, swimming, and celebrating children's birthdays together, to now being able to eat hot pot, drink wine, and talk late at night at home, this relationship has developed naturally.
markdown:
![image]()
Last weekend, we made an appointment with one of them to come to our house for hot pot.
It's said to be an "appointment", but actually it's not that formal. The other party's parents said they wanted to have hot pot tonight, and my wife immediately answered, so we might as well eat together. This is the characteristic of family social interaction with children - short decision-making cycle, fast execution, and not so much politeness and hesitation. Eat as much as you want. The kids are having fun together and the adults don’t have to sit around and check their phones.
My mother hurried to the vegetable market. I bought vegetables and tofu skin, but the beef was gone - the beef in the vegetable market is always gone when you need it. This is probably a branch of Murphy's law. So the task was transferred to me, I went to Hema NB to buy beef rolls.
There are really many people in Hema NB. I heard before that Hema's business was not doing well, with many stores closed, and it looked like it was going to be in trouble. But since I started doing Hema NB—the name has always seemed subtle to me, like a self-suggestion—the business suddenly came back to life. I was picking beef rolls in front of the freezer, and an old man next to me was studying the price tags of mutton rolls, muttering, "This one is expensive, that one is expensive, they are all expensive." I sympathized deeply, but grabbed two boxes of beef rolls and threw them into my shopping cart.
Passing by the seafood area, I remembered that my wife loves salmon, so I grabbed a box. At this time, you will have the illusion that you are a good husband, even though you only spent dozens of dollars more.
When I walked to the drinks area, I saw a can of Longjing-style craft beer. Longjing flavor, this concept is very abstract. I tried to imagine what the combination of Longjing tea and beer would taste like, but my imagination was limited. I could only take out my mobile phone and confirm with the other party's father, "Shall we have a drink?" The other party replied instantly, "Okay." So I bought two cans.
## Hotpot Gudu Gudu
The hot pot was steaming.
The children were playing with toys in the living room, running over from time to time to pick up some food, and then running back to continue playing. We adults were sitting at the dining table, chatting about everything from parenting experiences to interesting things about work, from the latest news to our own little troubles.
Although we are not in the same industry, there is no such "awkward chat" feeling at all. The topics came one after another, and the laughter came one after another. After drinking some wine - the can of Longjing-style craft beer does have a tea aroma, but more of a beer aroma - the atmosphere became more relaxed and the conversation became more open-minded.
I remember a moment when we were talking about our plans for our children after school, and suddenly realized that it was already past eleven o'clock.
"If the kids didn't have to go to school tomorrow, we might still be able to talk." The other party said this before leaving.
I particularly agree.
## Speaking of
Speaking of which, we have known each other for more than a year.
One weekend afternoon last year, I was taking my child to play downstairs, and the child ran to another child, and the two of them quickly played together. The child's parents and I naturally started chatting - starting from "How old is your child?", talking about kindergarten, talking about where to go to play on weekends, and talking about various little worries about parenting.
At that time, I never imagined that this chance encounter would turn into such a close relationship.
Later we went camping together, swam together, and celebrated our children’s birthdays together. In every activity, the children had great fun, and we adults became more and more familiar with it. From the initial "a few chats while walking the baby", to now we can talk about family, work and life. The change of this relationship is natural, without deliberateness and no sense of distance.
## About making friends
When I was a child in the village, basically everyone in the village knew each other. Everyone knows how many people live in each family, how old their children are, and what happy events their family has recently. It was very natural to make friends at that time. You could meet acquaintances when you went out, and you could have a lot of fun chatting just a few words.
But what about now? After going to work, I don’t even know anyone on the first floor. I go in and out every day, and when I bump into neighbors in the elevator, I at most nod, say "hello", and then go home and close the door.
Sometimes I also wonder, do we not like to make friends?
But thinking about it carefully, it seems that is not the case. If it weren't for my children, I probably wouldn't take the initiative to meet new friends. It's not that I don't want to, it's that there seems to be no opportunity and no reason. Everyone is very busy and has their own life, and there seems to be no need to deliberately socialize.
But in fact? I can feel that everyone still needs friends. Just like this hot pot game, we chatted so happily and laughed so relaxedly. The feeling was real and from the heart. Talking and laughing together, raising children together, and sharing every bit of life together, isn't this what we need?
Maybe modern life has caused us to lose some natural social scenes, but fortunately, children give us a chance to re-establish connections.
## Postscript
After writing this article, I thought of that hot pot restaurant again. The hot pot was sizzling, the children were laughing and joking, and we adults sat at the dining table and couldn't stop chatting.
That feeling is really good.
Thanks to the children, we have made these friends. Thanks to these friends, the journey of raising a baby is no longer lonely.
By the way, that can of Longjing flavored craft beer does have a tea aroma.
